Definition: Amnon (or Aminon), a son of David
BiblicalUsage: Amnon was David's firstborn son, and his name is tied to one of the darkest stories in the family: he loved his half-sister Tamar, forced her, and then hated her, and two years later Absalom had his servants kill him at a feast, and the news reached David as though all his sons were dead. The Bible tells it plainly, without softening what Amnon did or what it cost.
TheologicalSignificance: What strikes me about Amnon is how fast lust turns to hate and how one sin drags a whole family down with it: David did nothing, Absalom took revenge, and the house never recovered. I believe the story is there so we see sin for what it is — not a private slip, but a fire that burns everyone near it.
